solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insect-catcher in two horse-drawn vehicles

indicators.note: says the phrase that follows names a pair of things, to be set side by side

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn carriage for hire
a trap is a small two-wheeled horse-drawn cart

explanation.surface: Something that catches insects travelling in a pair of horse-drawn carriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse-drawn vehicles' describes both carriages at once; 'two' asks for two of them, a fly and a trap, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant that snaps shut on insects that land on it.

clue.text: Cruel jerks making money

indicators.note: to jerk something is to jolt it about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Cruel people who jerk others about to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is a scornful word for money, as in 'filthy lucre', wealth gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Instruct the Queen: you may put your foot in it!

definitions.text: you may put your foot in it!

parts.note: to instruct someone is to train them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A command to teach the monarch, with a joke about putting your foot in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put your foot in it' looks like the idiom for blundering, but here it is literal: a trainer is a sports shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, which is literally something you slide your foot into.

clue.text: Help one to be inserted in publicity

indicators.note: says the next piece is placed inside the word for publicity

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a piece of publicity
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Assistance needed to slip something into an advertising campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and help are synonyms, as nouns or verbs: to give assistance.

clue.text: Present box unopened

indicators.note: a thing left unopened has lost its opening, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a coffer is a strong box for valuables

explanation.surface: A gift box that nobody has opened yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present box' reads as a gift box; 'Present' is the verb, the definition, and 'unopened' drops the C from COFFER.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to offer it, to hold it out for someone to accept.

clue.text: Fine taste shown in film

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a lick is a small taste of something

explanation.surface: Good taste on display in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Flick is informal slang for a film, from the flickering of early cinema images.

clue.text: Viewer hurt: it doesn't look good

parts.note: the eye is the organ that views things
sore means hurting, painful

explanation.surface: A spectator has been injured, and it isn't a pretty sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly, an unsightly building or object spoiling the view.

clue.text: Secret group bound to be reduced

parts.note: a clan is a group of families

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: bound to do something is destined to do it

explanation.surface: A secretive group certain to be cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means kept secret or done covertly, like a hidden meeting.

clue.text: Fabulous master embracing piano: one's sure to make an impression

definitions.text: one's sure to make an impression

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as arms hold someone
fabulous means invented, the stuff of fable, so these letters are made up anew

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A brilliant teacher who plays piano is certain to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' turns MASTER into STAMER, and 'embracing' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamper is a device or person that stamps, literally pressing an impression into a surface.

clue.text: Like enthusiast to some extent

indicators.note: only partly present, so the answer sits as a run of letters within the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somewhat like a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'extent' as the definition, which cannot mean the answer; the whole clue defines it, being like an enthusiast, while 'to some extent' signals the letters inside 'Like enthusiast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen is being eager and enthusiastic, exactly the quality an enthusiast has.

clue.text: What careless cook may do is eccentric

definitions.meaning: a clumsy cook might break, or crack, a cooking pot
an eccentric is an oddball, a crank with mad ideas

explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is a crazy or eccentric person, the pot being the head that is cracked.

clue.text: Sack finance department employee

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from service, especially an officer in disgrace
a person handling money in a bank or a company's accounts office

explanation.definitionFit: Cashier is both a verb for dismissing an officer and a noun for whoever handles cash payments.

clue.text: Good people left in two seconds

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, so two of them give a pair
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Decent folk who departed in a couple of moments.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is informally a good-natured, generous person, so good sports are decent people.

clue.text: A party vote below average is an apparent absurdity

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece below another is written after it

parts.note: par is the standard or average level
a do is a party or celebration
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A party's vote share has fallen below the norm, which seems ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradox is a statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd yet may hold true.

clue.text: Audience's disconcerted by stages

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: fazed means disconcerted or thrown

explanation.surface: Listeners were thrown off balance step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phased is introduced gradually, carried out in distinct steps.

clue.text: Still, Cockney's bald?

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a bald head has no hair

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Londoner has lost their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb; it is the adjective for calm weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Airless weather is still, with no breeze moving.

clue.text: Comparatively cool model retired around noon

indicators.note: the reworked letters surround the next piece
to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are refashioned

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram

explanation.surface: A model who has stopped working is more fashionable at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a noun but is the verb signalling that RETIRED is rearranged around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendier is the comparative of trendy, meaning more fashionable or cool.

clue.text: African antelope snared by many, alas

indicators.note: caught inside, so the answer lies trapped within the following words

explanation.surface: An antelope caught in traps set by many people, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

clue.text: Gown or doublet regularly chosen

indicators.note: letters are picked at even intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: Choosing between a gown and a doublet, as an Elizabethan dresser might.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose gown, as worn by judges or at ceremonies.

clue.text: No brother or sister mounting this buffalo

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing upward means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a sib, or sibling, is a brother or sister

explanation.surface: No sibling is riding this buffalo.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison is commonly called a buffalo.

clue.text: Identical twins no longer in the belfry?

parts.note: someone who is no longer alive is dead
bell-ringers are the people found in a church's bell tower

explanation.surface: Twins who are no longer up in the bell tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase is bellringers who have died.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead ringers are people who look exactly alike, the way identical twins do.

clue.text: Roll up for the most important part

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll

explanation.surface: Rolling up is what matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub is the central point or crux of a matter.

clue.text: Former postman, an exile

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
Postman Pat is the title character of a British children's TV series about a village postman

explanation.surface: A retired postman who now lives in exile.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, lives outside their native country, like an exile.

clue.text: One's rebuffed in a slam and that's humiliating

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the phrase that follows it

parts.note: a bang is a slam, as of a door

indicators.note: turned back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, I and the verb is

explanation.surface: Being turned away during a big slam is humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', I plus IS; 'rebuffed' sends it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasing means degrading or humbling someone, lowering their dignity.
